To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of a label on perceived ability to recovery from an illness or injury depends on whether the label is positive or negative, the type of illness or injury, and the type of label.

the label "chronic fatigue syndrome" (CFS) was perceived to indicate that the condition is more serious, more difficult to recover from, more likely to have a negative effect on the patient's life, and more likely to be a lifelong condition than the label "myalgic encephalomyelitis" (ME).
The effect of labeling on the perceived ability to recover was not consistent across illnesses and injuries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of labeling on people's perceptions of their own ability to recover from illness and injury.
the effect of the labeling of an illness or injury on the perceived ability to recover.
the effect of labeling on the perceived ability to recover and the effect of the perceived ability to recovery on actual recovery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of labeling on recovery of acute illnesses and injuries is not well established.
the effects of labeling in the context of acute illnesses or injuries are not as clear as they are in the case of chronic illness.
the effect of labeling on recovery is not as clear cut as the effect of labeling of mental illness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the effect of labeling on recovery from illness and injury depends on whether the label is positive or negative.
the effects of labeling are not always what one might expect.
the more labels a person is exposed to, the less likely they are to recover from an illness or injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need more research on the effect of labeling on people’s perceptions of their ability to recover from illness.
people are more likely to recover from illnesses and injuries when they are told that other people have recovered from similar illnesses and injuries.
people are less likely to seek medical care when they believe they can treat their illness or injury at home.
